([[Ramsey, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] (2018–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–{{nbay|2023|start}} | team1 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | years2 = 2022–2023 | team2 = → [[Raptors 905]] | years3 = 2024–2025 | team3 = [[Maine Celtics]] | years4 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team4 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | years5 = 2025 | team5 = → [[Motor City Cruise]] | years6 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team6 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years7 = 2025–2026 | team7 = → [[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League Third Team]] ([[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]) * Honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]] ([[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2022]]) * Second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2022) * Third-team All-Big Ten (2021) * [[Haggerty Award]] (2022) }} '''Ronald Harper Jr.''' (born April 12, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. He is the son of former NBA player [[Ron Harper]] and the older brother of [[San Antonio Spurs]] player [[Dylan Harper]]. ==Early life and high school career== Harper was born in [[Paterson, New Jersey]], while his father, [[Ron Harper]], was playing for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the NBA. He began playing basketball under the coaching of his mother, Maria.{{cite web |last=Flojo |first=Enzo |title=Son of a Bull |url=https://tribune.net.ph/index.php/2020/05/10/son-of-a-bull/ |work=[[Daily Tribune (Philippines)|Daily Tribune]] |date=May 10, 2020 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} On the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit, he played for Ring City Basketball, a program operated by his parents.{{cite news |title=Rising Fil-Am hoop star is from family of cagers |url=https://globalnation.inquirer.net/144715/rising-fil-am-hoop-star-is-from-family-of-cagers |newspaper=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |date=September 13, 2016 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} He was raised in [[Upper Saddle River, New Jersey|Upper Saddle River]] and [[Franklin Lakes, New Jersey]], and attended [[Don Bosco Preparatory High School]] in [[Ramsey, New Jersey]].{{cite news |last=Cooper |first=Darren |title=What's in a name, if it's Harper? |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/columnists/darren-cooper/2017/03/14/cooper-whats-name-if-s-harper/99186014/ |work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]] |date=March 14, 2017 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} As a junior, Harper averaged 10.1 points per game and helped Don Bosco win its first NJSIAA Non-Public A state championship in 47 years. During his senior season, he averaged 20.8 points and led the Ironmen to a 29–3 record, a second consecutive Non-Public A title and the Bergen County Jamboree championship.{{cite web |title=Ron Harper Jr. – Men's Basketball |url=https://scarletknights.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ron-harper-jr-/10593 |website=Rutgers University Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He was named North Jersey Player of the Year by ''The Record''.{{cite news |last=Mattura |first=Greg |title=North Jersey's All-Decade Boys Basketball Team |url=https://www.northjersey.com/story/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/2019/12/10/nj-boys-basketball-north-jersey-all-decade-team/4066499002/ |work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]] |date=December 10, 2019 |access-date=October 13, 2020}} Harper was rated a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. He committed to Rutgers on August 11, 2017, choosing the Scarlet Knights over reported offers that included [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] and [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (Ohio)]].{{cite news |last=Carino |first=Jerry |title=Rutgers basketball: Don Bosco wing Ron Harper Jr., son of NBA champ, commits |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2017/08/11/rutgers-basketball-don-bosco-wing-ron-harper-jr-son-nba-champ-commits/561474001/ |work=[[Asbury Park Press]] |date=August 11, 2017 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} ==College career== Harper appeared in all 31 games as a freshman at Rutgers, averaging 7.8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game. As a sophomore, he started every game and led the team in scoring at 12.1 points per game while averaging 5.8 rebounds. He was named honorable mention All-Big Ten and second-team All-Met.{{cite web |title=Ron Harper Jr. College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ron-harperjr-1.html |website=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} As a junior, Harper averaged 14.9 points and 5.9 rebounds and earned third-team All-Big Ten and first-team All-Met honors. He helped Rutgers qualify for its first [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] since 1991.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Punches Ticket to NCAA Tournament |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2021/3/14/mens-basketball-mens-basketball-punches-ticket-to-ncaa-tournament |website=Rutgers University Athletics |date=March 14, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Rutgers defeated [[Clemson Tigers men's basketball|Clemson]] in the first round for the program's first NCAA tournament victory since 1983.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Defeats Clemson in the NCAA Tournament |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2021/3/19/mens-basketball-recap-clemson-in-the-ncaa-tournament |website=Rutgers University Athletics |date=March 19, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Following the season, Harper entered the [[2021 NBA draft]] process before withdrawing and returning to Rutgers.{{cite web |title=Geo Baker and Ron Harper Jr. to Return to Rutgers Basketball |url=https://scarletknights.com/news/2021/7/7/mens-basketball-geo-baker-and-ron-harper-jr-to-return-to-rutgers-basketball |website=Rutgers University Athletics |date=July 7, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On December 9, 2021, Harper recorded 30 points and 10 rebounds against the top-ranked [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue Boilermakers]]. He made a shot from just inside halfcourt at the buzzer to give Rutgers a 70–68 victory, its first win over the No. 1-ranked team in program history.{{cite news |title=Harper connects at buzzer, Rutgers shocks No. 1 Purdue 70–68 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-basketball-mens-college-basketball-college-basketball-rutgers-scarlet-knights-mens-basketball-c1cc5b7b51395a2517fbf43b2544b31c |work=[[Associated Press|AP News]] |date=December 9, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} As a senior, he averaged 15.8 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. Harper was named second-team All-Big Ten,{{cite press release |title=2021–22 Big Ten Men's Basketball Postseason Honors Announced |url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |website=BigTen.org |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |access-date=March 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308180525/https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx |archive-date=March 8, 2022 |url-status=dead}} an AP honorable mention All-American and the recipient of the Haggerty Award as the leading Division I men's college basketball player in the New York metropolitan area.{{cite web |last=Corso |first=Chris |title=Ron Harper Jr. Wins the Haggerty Award, Geo Baker, Caleb McConnell also Honored by All-Met 2022 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Following Rutgers' loss in the First Four of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2022 NCAA tournament]], Harper announced that he would forgo his remaining collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Rutgers' Ron Harper Jr., a projected second-round pick, to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33578597/rutgers-ron-harper-jr-projected-second-round-pick-declare-nba-draft |website=ESPN.com |date=March 23, 2022 |access-date=March 23, 2022}} He went undrafted.{{cite news |last=Fonseca |first=Brian |title=How Ron Harper Jr., ex-Rutgers teammates reacted to him going undrafted |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2022/06/what-theyre-saying-about-ex-rutgers-star-ron-harper-jr-going-undrafted-signing-with-raptors.html |website=NJ.com |date=June 24, 2022 |access-date=June 24, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors and Raptors 905 (2022–2023)=== On July 14, 2022, Harper signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]] and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web |title=Raptors Sign Harper Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-harper-jr |website=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2022 |access-date=July 14, 2022}} He appeared in nine NBA games during his rookie season. On July 22, 2023, Harper signed another two-way contract with Toronto.{{cite web |title=Raptors Re-Sign Dowtin Jr. and Harper Jr. and Add Freeman-Liberty |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-re-sign-dowtin-jr-and-harper-jr-and-add-freeman-liberty |website=NBA.com |date=July 22, 2023 |access-date=July 22, 2023}} The Raptors waived him on December 8 after announcing that he would undergo season-ending shoulder surgery.{{cite web |title=Harper Jr. to Undergo Season-Ending Surgery |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/harper-jr-to-undergo-season-ending-surgery |website=NBA.com |date=December 8, 2023 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ===Maine Celtics (2024–2025)=== After playing for the [[Boston Celtics]] during the [[2024 NBA Summer League]], Harper signed an Exhibit 10 contract with Boston in July 2024.{{cite web |last=Barth |first=Alex |title=Celtics Summer League roster and schedule announced |url=https://985thesportshub.com/2024/07/08/celtics-summer-league-schedule/ |website=98.5 The Sports Hub |date=July 8, 2024 |access-date=August 31, 2024}}{{cite web |last=Kirschenbaum |first=Alex |title=Ron Harper Jr. Signs Camp Contract with Celtics |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/ron-harper-jr-signing-camp-contract-with-celtics.html |website=Hoops Rumors |date=July 14, 2024 |access-date=August 31, 2024}} He was waived on October 17,{{cite web |last=Tucker |first=Tristan |title=Celtics Waive Jay Scrubb, Ron Harper Jr., Hason Ward |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/celtics-waive-jay-scrubb-ron-harper-jr-hason-ward.html |website=Hoops Rumors |date=October 17, 2024 |access-date=October 18, 2024}} and joined the [[Maine Celtics]] on October 26.{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Spencer |title=Celtics Select Three in G League Draft |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/draft-training-camp-102624 |website=Maine Celtics |date=October 26, 2024 |access-date=October 26, 2024}} ===Detroit Pistons and Motor City Cruise (2025)=== On January 6, 2025, Harper signed a two-way contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]], joining their G League affiliate, the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Ron Harper Jr. to Two-Way Contract |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/detroit-pistons-sign-ron-harper-jr-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA G League |date=January 6, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On February 1, he made 11 of 18 three-point attempts in a 145–132 victory over the [[Long Island Nets]], setting a Cruise franchise record for three-pointers in a game.{{cite web |title=Long Island Nets at Motor City Cruise |url=https://gleague.nba.com/game/lin-vs-mcc-2022400216 |website=NBA G League |date=February 1, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Harper appeared in one NBA game for Detroit. The Pistons waived him on July 24.{{cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |title=Ron Harper Jr. Released by Pistons |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/ron-harper-jr-released-by-pistons.html |website=Hoops Rumors |date=July 24, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ===Boston Celtics and Maine Celtics (2025–present)=== In August 2025, Harper agreed to return to Boston on an Exhibit 10 contract.{{cite web |last=Dolloff |first=Matt |title=Celtics sign son of 5-time NBA champion to Exhibit 10 contract |url=https://985thesportshub.com/2025/08/18/celtics-ron-harper-jr-exhibit-10-contract/ |website=98.5 The Sports Hub |date=August 18, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On October 16, the Celtics converted his contract to a two-way deal.{{cite press release |title=Celtics Convert Ron Harper Jr. to Two-Way Contract |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/celtics-convert-ron-harper-jr-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA G League |date=October 16, 2025 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On February 4, 2026, Harper made his first NBA start and recorded 11 points, nine rebounds and three assists in a 114–93 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Spencer |title=Harper's first NBA start headlines big night for Maine's Two-Way players |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/ron-harper-jr-first-nba-career-start |website=Maine Celtics |date=February 5, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} In 18 games with Maine across the G League Tip-Off Tournament and regular season, all starts, he averaged 25.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.2 blocks in 31.2 minutes per game. He was selected to participate in the 2026 [[Rising Stars Challenge]] and was named to the All-NBA G League Third Team.{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Spencer |title=Harper Jr. named to All NBA G League Third Team |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/harper-jr-named-to-all-nba-g-league-third-team |website=Maine Celtics |date=April 7, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On April 4, Boston converted Harper's two-way contract to a standard NBA contract.{{cite press release |title=Ron Harper Jr. signs standard deal with Celtics |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/harper-jr-signs-standard-deal-with-celtics-04042025 |website=Maine Celtics |date=April 5, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} On April 12, his 26th birthday, he scored a career-high 27 points and added seven rebounds, four assists and three steals in a 113–108 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite news |last=Himmelsbach |first=Adam |title=With eight players resting, Celtics reserves pull off inspiring victory over play-in-bound Magic |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/04/12/sports/nba-celtics-magic-game-score-garza/ |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |date=April 12, 2026 |access-date=April 12, 2026}} Boston declined the team option in Harper's contract for the 2026–27 season before signing him to a new multiyear agreement on July 6.{{cite news |title=Report: Ron Harper Jr. to sign 3-year, $9M deal with Celtics |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/report-ron-harper-jr-sign-3-year-9m-deal-with-celtics--flm-2026-06-27/ |work=[[Reuters]] |date=June 27, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}{{cite press release |title=Celtics Sign Ron Harper Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260706-celtics-sign-ron-harper-jr |website=NBA.com |publisher=Boston Celtics |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}} The finalized contract was reported as worth up to $13.7 million over four years. Its first two seasons were fully guaranteed, while the third season was non-guaranteed and the fourth was a non-guaranteed team option.{{cite news |last=Thompson |first=Khari A. |title=Celtics sign Ron Harper Jr. to multi-year contract |url=https://www.boston.com/sports/boston-celtics/2026/07/07/celtics-sign-ron-harper-jr-multiyear-contract-comments/ |website=Boston.com |date=July 7, 2026 {{s-end}} ==Personal life== Harper's father, [[Ron Harper]], was an All-American college basketball player at [[Miami RedHawks men's basketball|Miami (Ohio)]] and played 15 seasons in the NBA, winning five championships.{{cite web |last=Politi |first=Steve |title=Like father, like son? Rutgers can only hope with Ron Harper Jr. |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2018/03/ron_harper_jr_rutgers_father_like_son_column_polit.html |website=NJ.com |date=March 11, 2018 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} His mother, Maria (née Pizarro), is of Filipino descent and played college basketball at the [[New Orleans Privateers women's basketball|University of New Orleans]]. She later coached the girls' basketball team at [[DePaul Catholic High School]] and served as an assistant coach for the boys' team at Don Bosco Prep.{{cite web |last=Davis |first=Seth |author-link=Seth Davis |title=How a mom's love helped Dylan Harper become top basketball recruit in Class of 2024 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4683552/2023/07/12/dylan-harper-basketball-recruiting-rutgers-duke/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |date=July 12, 2023 |access-date=July 18, 2023}} Harper's maternal grandfather, Manuel Pizarro, represented the Philippines in the [[Basque pelota]] demonstration event at the [[1968 Summer Olympics]].{{cite web |last=Fonseca |first=Brian |title='Address me by my name': Rutgers' Ron Harper Jr. goes one-on-one with his father's legacy |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2020/03/how-rutgers-ronald-harper-jr-is-building-a-name-for-himself.html |website=NJ.com |date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=October 12, 2020}} Harper has expressed interest in representing the [[Philippines men's national basketball team|Philippines national team]]. He attempted to obtain a Philippine passport while in high school, but the application was not completed.{{cite web |last=Henson |first=Joaquin M. |title=Harper's son open to play for Gilas |url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2021/12/09/2146670/harpers-son-open-play-gilas |website=[[The Philippine Star|Philstar.com]] |date=December 9, 2021 |access-date=December 8, 2024}} His younger brother, [[Dylan Harper]], played one season at Rutgers before being selected second overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite press release |title=Spurs Sign 2025 Second Overall Pick Dylan Harper |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-2025-second-overall-pick-dylan-harper |website=NBA.com |publisher=San Antonio Spurs |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==References==
